Full Review: When I visited Miri early this year all the way from the UK, I brought my family to Lao Yang as a treat as it had good reviews but was disappointed as all the dimsum served was cold!! How could anyone serve cold dimsum?? So this time I decided to try Han Palace and brought my family for dimsum today and it was good. We enjoyed the Lao Sha Bao, sweet and sour roll and the cheung fun. We ordered kueh tiaw basah as well which was actually cooked like wat tan hor and that was quite good too. We were initially quite apprehensive about it being halal, meaning the cha siew bao has chicken filling instead of pork and they don't serve cha siew cheung fun. However we were pleasantly surprised how good the "cha siew bao" was. They refilled tea for free too. Overall it was a better experience than Lao Yang; at least the dimsum was warm. Definitely will come back here again with my family. One other thing was that most of the fried dimsum was not available as they finished selling them over the weekend! Apparently this is a frequent occurrence and so would advise to avoid Mondays if you want the full selection of dimsum.

Full Review: When in Malacca I wouldn't missed my makan for the world be it lunch or dinner at any of the peranakan restaurants that have been mushrooming all over Malacca particularly in Taman Melaka Raya. I simply take a leisurely stroll from Hatten hotel to my all-time favourite true blue peranakan Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine. I can't help but noticed the menu was laminated and new compared the previous one was old and looked antique enough to be sent to Malacca museum for preservation. Again the over-friendly Amy's husband passed the menu and before he could recommend the dishes; I reminded him this wasn't my first time. We ordered our best-loved ayam buah keluak, kerabu bendi (steamed lady's finger top with fresh red chillies shallots and daun limau perut) my personal favourite die die must order. For prawn we tried the sambal tumis udang with petai. We did not call in advance to make reservations which normally is a must if you do not wish to go all the way and be disappointed if the restaurant is fully-booked. We were lucky as we arrived at 6.30pm though there were already walk-in diners but most tables were reserved. Since only the two of us, he was kind enough to accomodate us with a table brought from outside the restaurant set up near the entrance.All the the three dishes served on out tables less than 15minutes. After the last time early last year we had the same food especially ayam buah keluak and the steamed bendi was still superbly good though the sambal udang prawn with petai "not soo pedas". Maybe Amy trying to tone down the spiciness of the sambal tumis. Honestly still the best nyonya food I have had in Malacca and I promised uncle Lim...I'll be back!!!

Full Review: It was a weekend of makan (eat) and shopping spree in Melaka and Amy Heritage Nonya Cuisine) was on our check list. Having made advance reservation via a phone call. We were not disappointed with our lunch there. The kueh pie were tasty. The assam ikan was sedap too and so was the udang (prawns) masak nanas. The nonya mee was very sedap very similiar to my mum's home cooked version. The chicken cooked with candle nut (buah keras) was yummy. But the otak was a disappointment, as the rempah has a very strong kunyit (turmeric) taste which overwhelm the flavour. The chap chye was disappointing, the gravy was too sweet and the cabbage was hard. We had chendol for dessert and it was ok. The gula melaka was very wangi (fragrant) but quite diluted. Using freshly squeezed coconut (santan) would have enhanced the flavour further. Overall we enjoyed the lunch very much. And will return to try the buah keluak and other nonya dishes. A note of advice. Do call to make reservation at least a day or two in advance.

The grill (we paid more for dinner bcoz of the grill) was also cold. Cold chicken wings and hard chewy gummy lamb. The dessert spread was lean with only malay kueh kueh (cakes) which looks like it had been left on the buffet since lunch.10. I had a little bit of diarrhoea when I got back to the hotel.So if you really must go to WASTE your money and experience HORRIBLE Food and ATROCIOUS Service, perhaps you can go during lunch when the food is hot and freshly prepared or when the Chef is in-house (I suppose). For RM43/person, you can enjoy a much better dinner at anywhere else in KL for half the price.In short, Indah Kata dari Rasa! (Words are better than the real stuff)

Full Review: Back in the 90s and early 2000, Lok Thian is the household name and the go to place for makan. Dim sum, Chinese, Japanese or Thai cuisines...their restaurant used to be the place be. But these days...service wise is really bad. On Christmas morning we decided to have brunch with the in-laws. They arrived first and were seated upstairs but nobody came to take their order, my sister in-law went downstairs to order but was chased back up. When we arrived, we took the liberty to go back down to place our order. After placing our orders we sat and waited. Only some of our orders arrived and the drinks came very late. After waiting for some time and our food didn't seem to be coming we decided to leave and when we went to pay they had the audacity to charge us for the food which weren't served. Only after insisting we didn't get the food did they later waived the amount. We  came to support local businesses and as the world is opening up more people are going out to eat with family and friends yet they don't seem to have enough staff to take orders and serve food.  How to help such local businesses when they don't help themselves to improve and deliver quality service? Really spoil our mood for the day. I'll think twice if I ever have to come here in the future...

Full Review: I grew up eating here. My personal childhood favourite was Uncle "Lek Koo"s beef soup noodles - with beef balls, tender beef strips served with real beef broth - he'd have none of the ajinomoto version. New Hollywood used to have a real grumpy popiah basah uncle who would only sell you his popiah if he was in a good mood. But his popiah was so good, folks would put up with his bad moods just to have it. Now Uncle "Lek Koo" and the grumpy popiah man are no longer around - well at least not when i went there last week - but the food is still great. New Hollywood also still serves the famous Ipoh egg caramel custard. The roti telur goyang. The char kway teow is also very nice. I enjoyed the Siamese laksa on that Sunday. Apparently the brother of HRH the late Sultan of Perak lives further down the road from this kedai kopi and some members of the Perak royal family makan here too. And yes, it's all halal. It reminds me of the old days when Malaysians of all races and religions could eat together in a kopitiam.
